title: Single Number / XOR Cancellation
contract: Every integer appears exactly twice except one appearing once. Return that unique integer; input is nonempty.
brute: for(int x:a){int count=0;for(int y:a)if(x==y)count++;emit("Count one candidate","value",x,"occurrences",count);if(count==1)return x;}throw new IllegalArgumentException("Contract violated");
optimal: int value=0;for(int x:a){value^=x;emit("Equal pairs cancel under XOR","value",x,"accumulator",value);}return value;
reasoning: Count each candidate and stop when its frequency is one.
XOR is associative and commutative, x XOR x = 0, and x XOR 0 = x.
All duplicated values cancel, leaving the unique value. The frequency contract is essential: this does not solve arbitrary odd-frequency cases with several unique values.
